title: Governor’s Commission on School Construction
before:
Per an executive order signed by Gov. Janet Mills, the Governor’s Commission on School Construction will review school construction needs throughout the State of Maine, existing programs that address school facilities needs, and potential new approaches for increasing equity and overall impact. This will be the first such effort in more than 25 years.

Since 2019, the Mills Administration, in partnership with the Maine Legislature, has provided an unprecedented $580 million to finance the renovation and construction of Maine schools. Despite these record investments, the need for construction and renovation of public school facilities in the State has far outpaced available capacity. Additionally, in the years ahead, Maine’s aging school infrastructure is expected to require even more investment.  

Maine students and educators deserve safe, healthy, comfortable, quiet, technology-friendly, functional buildings. The Commission will bring together state, municipal, and education leaders to provide a report with recommendations that outline school construction and renovation needs based on existing data and through input from stakeholders; provide analysis summarizing how other states fund and operate programs supporting public school facilities; and identify potential changes to current state law, rules, and policies controlling school construction.  

Members of the Commission include:  

  • Pender Makin, Commissioner of the Maine Department of Education 
  • Valerie Landry, Chair of the Commission 
  • Jenny Boyden, Associate Commissioner of the Maine Department of Administrative and Financial Services 
  • Elaine Clark, Acting Director of the State Bureau of General Services 
  • Hollis Cobb, Tri-State Committee member of the Maine Association of School Business Officials 
  • Fern Desjardins, Chair of the Maine State Board of Education 
  • Art Dudley, President of Arthur C. Dudley Contractor-Builder Inc.  
  • Roy Gott, Member of the RSU 24 (Sullivan) School Board 
  • Chris Howell, Superintendent of RSU 14 (Windham)  
  • Anthony Jaccarino, Investment Officer for all of the Authorities, Maine Municipal Bond Bank 
  • Jane McCall, Superintendent of RSU 39 (Caribou) 
  • Justin Poirier, Member of the Maine Municipal Association 
  • Rhonda Sperrey, Superintendent of RSU 64 (Corinth) 

On April 15, 2025, the Commission issued an Interim Summary of the information and issues reviewed by the Commission thus far. Given the scope and depth of the issues still before the Commission, and in consultation with the Governor’s Office, the Commission will continue its work through 2025, delivering a full and final report—including recommendations—later in the year.

Comments/Questions 

You may submit comments or questions for the Commission to consider in the form below. Public input and questions will be summarized for Commission members at each meeting.

notes: 790 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 2 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "Related Legislation" is an h4 with no h3 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 4 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Give the sub-headings their rule
decisions.why: 2 sub-headings are plain bold text. The design has a treatment for them — a teal rule down the left and a line across — and it had never been used on any page, because it needs a wrapper an author would have to know about.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 2 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 2 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
